title: Negative: a CIPS predator (second enzyme condensing by catalysis that digests c40's CIPS prey enzyme) never condenses; its uniform bath level dissolves the prey condensates first (18 runs, 128^2)
summary: world.py adds to c40's catalysis-induced condensates (prey enzyme e on a consumed, regrowing fuel; Lsc 2 at 128^2, which gives 3-5 dividing prey bodies alone, screen/prey_only.png) a predator enzyme q made everywhere by turnover, drifting up its own product r, whose catalysis kr e^ne q^mq (1-r) consumes prey enzyme at yield y2. With q present from t=0 (q0 0.015-0.06, chiq 3-8, y2 0.5-1, ne 1) no prey body ever nucleates. With predation cooperative in the prey enzyme (ne 2) and q0 0.08-0.15, prey still never form. Introducing q at t=3000, after the prey have formed (q0 0.06-0.15, chiq 6-20, y2 0.1-0.3, mq 2-4, kr 2-50, q noise 0.02-0.08), dissolves every prey body within ~100 t while q stays at its bath level (max q = q0 at all times, screen/g4_counts.png): the predator eats as a uniform solution, not as condensed individuals. CIPS prey are marginally stable (c40's bath is linearly stable and bodies dissolve within 100 t when fuel stops), so any distributed enzyme loss larger than their turnover supply kills them, while a predator enzyme dilute enough to spare them is far below its own CIPS threshold (chiq q dr/dq < Dq). A working version probably needs predators that are planted as condensates, or a prey that survives a distributed loss (for example c36/c42's Cahn-Hilliard prey).

finding.operator: catalysis-induced phase separation of a predator enzyme driven by digesting the prey enzyme
finding.control: prey-only twin (pred_on 0) and 17 predator parameter sets, seed 0, 128^2, t=8000-10000
finding.result: prey-only: 3-5 prey bodies; every predator arm: 0 predator condensates (q max = q0), prey 0-1 bodies at the end; with predators introduced at t=3000 the 3 prey bodies dissolve by t=3100
